question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-declaration path ownership plus the proposed bounded `tools.allow` and `tools.deny` tightening as the permanent V1 managed-configuration security contract?
rationale: Runtime proof can validate the implementation, but it cannot decide whether these precedence and policy-composition semantics are the permanent core contract maintainers want to support.

options.title: Approve the V1 contract
options.body: Accept the startup-only immutable layering contract after confirming implementation parity and recording the maintainer-discussion decision.

options.title: Narrow policy composition
options.body: Retain generic ordered layers but remove or revise special tool-policy behavior until those security semantics receive separate approval.

options.title: Keep composition host-owned
options.body: Decline the new core seam and leave configuration composition to host supervisors such as Lobster.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept the startup-only immutable layering contract after confirming implementation parity and recording the maintainer-discussion decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline directly routes the RFC to steipete, and this decision combines core product acceptance with configuration-boundary ownership.
